column1: # comment: "Data-quality layer alignments \u2014 ISO 19157 dimensions + lineage, bridged to W3C DQV and GeoDCAT-AP by reference. FORMAL GROUNDING: gmeow:QualityAssessment is a gufo:SubKind of gmeow:Observation, reusing the universal claim construct. gmeow:QualityDimension is a gufo:AbstractIndividualType / QualityValue \u2014 an open value vocabulary of individuals (never subclasses). There is no 'primary' or 'preferred' dimension (Principle 9). DQV FLATTENING: DQV introduces dqv:Metric between QualityMeasurement and Dimension. GMEOW flattens this (qualityDimension points directly to QualityDimension) because metric-specific metadata (thresholds, algorithms) are solver-layer concerns (Principle 12). The projection layer can expand to the full DQV chain when needed. ISO 19157 STATUS: ISO 19157:2013 defines completeness, logical consistency, positional accuracy, temporal accuracy, and thematic accuracy. No canonical RDF namespace exists for these dimensions; the mapping set documents their correspondence to GMEOW value individuals in the comment below. GeoDCAT-AP (http://data.europa.eu/r5r/) provides dcat:qualityAnnotation as the RDF-aligned pathway to ISO 19115/19157 quality and lineage concepts."
# # ISO 19157 dimension value correspondences (no canonical RDF IRIs; documented as comments):

# # REFUSED (Principle 5 — no faithful external term): gmeow:assessedEntity has no direct DQV counterpart. DQV's dqv:computedOn expects dcat:Dataset/Distribution; GMEOW's range is gmeow:Entity (universal). The closeMatch to dqv:computedOn is annotated with a scope note.

# # REFUSED (Principle 5): gmeow:qualityDimension has no exact DQV property. dqv:isMeasurementOf points to dqv:Metric, not directly to dqv:Dimension; the closeMatch carries a note about the flattening.

column7: Both are reified quality assessments carrying a numeric or categorical result. GMEOW's result is a ScalarQuantity bundle (unit+frame+determinacy+provenance); DQV uses dqv:value with an expectedDataType on the Metric.

DQV QualityAnnotation (a subclass of oa:Annotation) is broader — it covers ratings, certificates, and feedback, not only structured measurements. A GMEOW QualityAssessment MAY be projected to a DQV QualityAnnotation when the result is categorical or subjective.

GeoDCAT-AP represents quality statements as dcat:qualityAnnotation pointing to oa:Annotation. GMEOW's structured QualityAssessment can be projected to an OA Annotation when targeting GeoDCAT-AP consumers.
Both are quality dimensions — criteria for assessing data quality. GMEOW models dimensions as value individuals (gufo:QualityValue), not as OWL classes.
The entity whose quality is assessed. DQV's dqv:computedOn is generally scoped to dcat:Dataset/Distribution; GMEOW's assessedEntity is universal (any gmeow:Entity).

GMEOW flattens the DQV chain: qualityDimension points directly to QualityDimension, bypassing the intermediate dqv:Metric node. The metric is solver-computed and lives outside the OWL core (Principle 12).
Wikidata 'provenance' is the closest structured term for lineage; lineage is a quality-lens view of provenance.

Lineage is provenance viewed through a quality lens. GMEOW records structural lineage via wasDerivedFrom / wasGeneratedBy / ImportActivity (provenance module); the qualityDimensionLineage value marks an assessment that evaluates lineage completeness or correctness.
Wikidata 'spatial resolution' is the closest structured term for positional accuracy; it is broader (includes granularity) but captures the same spatial-quality axis.
